frameworks.title: Word order: SOV
frameworks.body: Bengali puts the verb at the END. 'I rice eat' instead of 'I eat rice'. The same pattern as Hindi and Urdu — once you master one, the others click faster.

frameworks.title: Three levels of 'you'
frameworks.body: তুই (intimate/close), তুমি (familiar), আপনি (formal). Use তুই only with very close friends or younger family — using it with a stranger is rude.

frameworks.title: No grammatical gender
frameworks.body: Unlike Urdu and Hindi, Bengali nouns don't have gender. সে means both 'he' and 'she'. Major simplification compared to its sister languages.

frameworks.title: Bangla script is phonetic
frameworks.body: Each letter represents one sound. Once you learn the script (about 50 characters), you can pronounce ANY Bengali word — no spelling chaos like English.

vocab.note: Widely used for a grandfather on either side in everyday speech; the formal terms distinguish them.
